page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-192 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8581C processors operating at 2.3 GHz. The configuration delivers 192 virtual CPUs across 96 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, supported by 720 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This server does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, ranking in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench, and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, achieving top-tier read speeds of up to 12,787.43 GB/sec for cached blocks and 577.03 GB/sec for uncached blocks. However, single-core CPU performance and overall Passmark memory scores remain in the average tier. Cryptographic and vector-heavy workloads benefit from hardware-accelerated instructions, as evidenced by top-tier scores in Passmark encryption and ray tracing benchmarks.

The resource profile of this instance offers high compute density for parallelized workloads, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient choice for large-scale deployments that do not require local NVMe storage. It is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM inference, where its AMX and AVX-512 capabilities can be fully utilized. Conversely, workloads dependent on high single-core performance or local disk I/O may encounter bottlenecks due to the average single-core metrics and the absence of local storage.
